symbols.name: \(\underline p\)
symbols.def: A common lower bound on all observed-cell probabilities in a positive-law neighborhood.

symbols.name: \(\epsilon\)
symbols.def: Arbitrary radius in the fiber-boundary predicate.

symbols.name: \(K\)
symbols.def: Number of cells of \(O\), equal to \(32\).

symbols.name: \(c_{K,n,\alpha}\)
symbols.def: Smallest constant whose Hellinger ball centered at the empirical \(K\)-cell law has uniform coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) under sample size \(n\).

symbols.name: \(c_\alpha\)
symbols.def: A constant depending only on \(K\) and \(\alpha\) in the two-law lower bound.

symbols.name: \(C_\alpha\)
symbols.def: A constant depending only on \(K\) and \(\alpha\) in the confidence-fiber upper bound.

symbols.name: \(\delta_\alpha\)
symbols.def: A constant depending only on \(K\) and \(\alpha\) in the Le Cam lower bound.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{WBC}}\)
symbols.def: Arrows are \(A\to H,Z,M,Y\), \(H\to Z,W,M,Y\), \(M\to Y\), and \(W\to Y\); districts are \(\{\{A\},\{H,Y\},\{Z\},\{W\},\{M\}\}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal S\)
symbols.def: Generic SCM with independent exogenous variables across districts.

symbols.name: \(Q_0\)
symbols.def: Source law in an ordered pair.

symbols.name: \(Q_1\)
symbols.def: Target law in an ordered pair.

symbols.name: \(\psi(\mathcal S)\)
symbols.def: \(\psi(\mathcal S)=\mathbb E_{\mathcal S}[Y_{0,H_0,M_{1,H_0},W_{H_0}}]\), using the same unit-level \(H_0\) throughout.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal R_D\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R_{D_A}=\mathcal A\); \(r_{HY}\) contains \(h_{r_{HY}}(a),y_{r_{HY}}(a,h,m,w)\), and the other schedules contain \(z_{r_Z}(a,h),w_{r_W}(h),m_{r_M}(a,h)\).

symbols.name: \(q(v)\)
symbols.def: \(q(v)=\sum_{r_A,r_{HY},r_Z,r_W,r_M}\lambda^A_{r_A}\lambda^{HY}_{r_{HY}}\lambda^Z_{r_Z}\lambda^W_{r_W}\lambda^M_{r_M}y_{r_{HY}}(0,h_{r_{HY}}(0),m_{r_M}(1,h_{r_{HY}}(0)),w_{r_W}(h_{r_{HY}}(0)))\). The shared \(h_{r_{HY}}(0)\) enforces one unit-level \(H_0\), and \(\sum_{r_A}\lambda^A_{r_A}=1\) removes the root factor from the interventional query.

symbols.name: \(\mathbb B\)
symbols.def: Product simplex for all five district masses.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal P_{\mathfrak M}^{+}\)
symbols.def: \(\{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathfrak M}:P(o)>0\text{ for every observed cell }o\}\).

symbols.name: \(t\)
symbols.def: Generic value of the causal query.

symbols.name: \(u\)
symbols.def: Perturbation coordinate used to test fiber boundaries.

symbols.name: \(C\)
symbols.space: relatively open connected semialgebraic subsets of \(\mathcal P_{\mathfrak M}^{+}\)
symbols.def: A cell in a finite semialgebraic partition compatible with the graph and boundary family of \(E_{\mathrm{WBC}}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal G_C(P)\)
symbols.def: Conjunction of a complete collection of \(P\)-only polynomial sign conditions defining \(C\), when such a collection is supplied.

symbols.name: \(R_{\mathrm{WBC},C}(P,t)\)
symbols.def: Square-free product of all \(t\)-dependent boundary polynomials in a supplied complete boundary representation on \(C\), required to exhaust the unrestricted fiber boundary.

symbols.name: \(b_j(P)\)
symbols.def: The \(j\)-th ordered simple real root branch of a supplied \(R_{\mathrm{WBC},C}(P,\cdot)\), selected by a Thom encoding.

symbols.name: \(\operatorname{TCalm}_q(P)\)
symbols.def: There are \(\kappa,r_0>0\) such that \(d_{\mathrm H}(q(\mathcal F(Q)),q(\mathcal F(P)))\le\kappa H(Q,P)\) for every feasible \(Q\) with \(H(Q,P)\le r_0\).

symbols.name: \(\operatorname{Rob}_{\mathrm{full}}(P)\)
symbols.def: Robinson's constraint qualification holds at every \(v\in\mathcal F(P)\) for the full response-fiber system.

symbols.name: \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{proj}}\)
symbols.def: Eliminate latent multipliers from intrinsic limiting-normal and active-set conditions for the \(q\)-projected response system.

standard.name: Wu--Bai--Cui hidden-recanting proxy graph, finite specialization
Robinson condition at every point of a feasible fiber

definitions.name: Hidden-recanting SCM class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M=\{\mathcal S:\mathcal S\models\mathcal G_{\mathrm{WBC}}\text{ and }P_{\mathcal S}^{O}(A=a)>0\text{ for every }a\in\mathcal A\}\).

definitions.name: Observable WBC fiber boundary
definitions.construction: \(E_{\mathrm{WBC}}(P,t)\iff (P,t)\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{WBC}}\text{ and }\forall\epsilon>0\;\exists u\in\mathbb R\text{ such that }|u-t|<\epsilon\text{ and }(P,u)\notin\Gamma_{\mathrm{WBC}}\).

definitions.name: Conditional WBC boundary representation
definitions.construction: Apply quantifier elimination to the fixed five-district formula \(E_{\mathrm{WBC}}(P,t)\), Hardt local triviality, and effective compatible stratification to obtain the existence of a finite semialgebraic partition with compatible boundary descriptions. Conditional on an externally supplied complete representation on a cell \(C\), let \(\mathcal G_C(P)\) contain every \(P\)-only sign guard, let \(R_{\mathrm{WBC},C}(P,t)\) be the square-free product of all \(t\)-dependent boundary polynomials whose branches exhaust the unrestricted fiber boundary, and set \(\Delta_{\mathrm{WBC},C}(P)=\operatorname{lc}_t(R_{\mathrm{WBC},C})(P)\operatorname{Disc}_t(R_{\mathrm{WBC},C}(P,\cdot))\).

definitions.name: Exact multinomial confidence fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_n=\{Q:H(Q,\widehat P_n)\le c_{K,n,\alpha}/\sqrt n\}\), where \(c_{K,n,\alpha}\) is calibrated by exact finite multinomial enumeration uniformly over \(Q\).

definitions.name: NPM-CERT
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{NPM\text{-}CERT}(P,r,\varepsilon)\) uses Duarte et al., Algorithm 2, moment--SOS and interval branch-and-bound in the style of Algorithm 3, and CAD. It returns real-algebraic feasible codes with isolating intervals and sign certificates, reconstructed SCMs, and rational inner and outer objective bounds within \(\varepsilon\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathfrak M}\), Duarte et al.'s Algorithm 2 and Theorem 1 specialized to the five districts give \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{WBC}}(P)=\Theta(P)=\{q(v):v\in\mathcal F(P)\}\). The factor \(\lambda^A_a=P(A=a)>0\) occurs in every observed-cell polynomial and sums out of \(q(v)\); every feasible code reconstructs an SCM with one shared \(H_0\). The compact image need not be an interval.
statements.justification: This supporting result fixes the observable graph and reconstructible witnesses used by the geometric theorem.
statements.gap: DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024 already proves general sharp equivalence; this is only its correctly coded graph-and-query specialization.
statements.consumer: It supplies the sharp-set map for the NLSY97 tracking-to-wage analysis.

statements.statement: Swapping \(Q_0,Q_1\) preserves the feasible ordered-pair set, so \(\Omega_P^{\to}(r)\) equals the supremum of \(d_{\mathrm H}(\Theta(Q_0),\Theta(Q_1))\) under the same three Hellinger restrictions.
statements.justification: The identity links directed excess to familiar Hausdorff continuity.
statements.gap: BeresteanuMolinari2008 uses both distances but not this ordered two-law causal modulus.
statements.consumer: The endpoint criterion and the minimax transfer use the same loss orientation.

statements.statement: For the fixed five-district response program, \(E_{\mathrm{WBC}}(P,t)\) is semialgebraic. Quantifier elimination, Hardt local triviality, and effective compatible stratification imply that \(\mathcal P_{\mathfrak M}^{+}\) admits a finite semialgebraic partition whose cells have compatible semialgebraic descriptions of the unrestricted fiber boundary. Now fix a cell \(C\) and condition on a supplied complete square-free boundary representation \(\{\mathcal G_C,R_{\mathrm{WBC},C}\}\) whose guards define \(C\) and whose branches exhaust the boundary of \(\Theta(Q)\) for every feasible \(Q\) in a neighborhood of \(P\). If \(P\) lies in the relative interior of \(C\) and \(\Delta_{\mathrm{WBC},C}(P)\ne0\), then every boundary point of \(\Theta(P)\) is a simple Nash root \(b_j(P)\), the roots continue without collision, and the interval-and-point incidence pattern is locally constant. For sufficiently small \(\eta>0\), every observed cell is at least \(\underline p>0\), \(\|Q_0-Q_1\|_2/\sqrt8\le H(Q_0,Q_1)\le\|Q_0-Q_1\|_2/\sqrt{8\underline p}\), and the implicit-root derivatives give \(d_{\mathrm H}(\Theta(Q_0),\Theta(Q_1))\le\kappa_C(P,\eta)H(Q_0,Q_1)\) whenever \(H(Q_j,P)\le\eta\). Under this supplied representation, \(\operatorname{TCalm}_q(P)\) holds and \(\Omega_P^{\to}(r)=O(r)\).
statements.justification: This letter-tier theorem records the graph-specialized existence result and isolates the exact additional certificate needed for a quantitative projected-calmness conclusion.
statements.gap: HelmerLeykinNanda2023, Theorem 4.5 and Theorem 5.4, already provides effective stratification machinery for real algebraic maps and full semialgebraic sets, while Hardt1980 supplies finite semialgebraic partitions with locally trivial fibers. DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024 already gives the response-program construction and sharp equivalence. These results yield the existence portion, but none supplies a computed unrestricted WBC boundary eliminant, complete observable guards, a nonzero discriminant evaluation, or the branch-exhaustion premise needed for the conditional Hausdorff bound.
statements.consumer: A future full-fiber certificate could instantiate the conditional implication at an NLSY97 fitted law; the present theorem does not provide that certificate.

statements.statement: For rational feasible \(P,r,\varepsilon\), \(\mathsf{NPM\text{-}CERT}\) terminates for extrema of \(q(\mathcal F(P))\) and for \(\Omega_P^{\to}(r)\), returning real-algebraic feasible codes with isolating intervals and sign certificates, reconstructed SCM witnesses, and rational inner and outer objective bounds within \(\varepsilon\).
statements.justification: This supporting result separates causal width from numerical error.
statements.gap: DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024 assigns construction to Algorithm 2, sharpness to Theorem 1, and anytime optimization to Algorithm 3; coupled Hellinger certification and exact witness representation are added here.
statements.consumer: Software can report checkable brackets and compatible SCM witnesses.

statements.statement: For every \(n\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathfrak M}}P^n\{\Theta(P)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_n\}\ge1-\alpha\). This includes simplex faces and rank-deficient proxy channels; outward \(\varepsilon\)-certificates preserve coverage.
statements.justification: Exact fiber inversion supplies the honest upper procedure used to interpret the elbow.
statements.gap: SachsGabrielFay2024 treats scalar multinomial functionals and RomanoShaikh2010 broad identified-set inference; this records the finite-sample whole-image implication for the fixed graph.
statements.consumer: It covers every compatible NLSY97 path-specific value.

statements.statement: There are constants \(c_\alpha,C_\alpha,\delta_\alpha>0\), depending only on \(K,\alpha\), such that \(P^n\{\Theta(P)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_n,\ \rho(\widehat\Theta_n,\Theta(P))\le\Omega_P^{\to}(C_\alpha n^{-1/2})\}\ge1-\alpha\). If a random closed set \(\widetilde\Theta_n\) is honest in the explicit neighborhood, meaning \(\inf_{Q:H(Q,P)\le c_\alpha n^{-1/2}}Q^n\{\Theta(Q)\subseteq\widetilde\Theta_n\}\ge1-\alpha\), then some feasible \(Q\) in that neighborhood satisfies \(Q^n\{\rho(\widetilde\Theta_n,\Theta(Q))\ge\Omega_P^{\to}(c_\alpha n^{-1/2})/4\}\ge\delta_\alpha\). At a law for which the complete unrestricted boundary representation and nonzero-discriminant premises of \(\mathrm{thm:wbc\text{-}observable\text{-}endpoint\text{-}eliminant\) have been independently certified, the upper enlargement is \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\); no matching root-\(n\) lower order is asserted without a corresponding modulus lower bound.
statements.justification: This supporting transfer gives the confidence-fiber upper bound and the two-law Le Cam lower bound under the same directed whole-set loss.
statements.gap: DonohoLiu1991, page 633 abstract, concerns scalar Hellinger moduli and testing; ArmstrongKolesar2018, Section 3.2 and Theorem 3.1 with Corollary 3.1, concerns ordered scalar moduli and confidence intervals over convex regression classes. Neither treats whole-set directed excess for this causal fiber image.
statements.consumer: The NLSY97 confidence region can report the modulus-governed honest enlargement benchmark and a certified root-\(n\) upper regime.

statements.statement: If \(\operatorname{Rob}_{\mathrm{full}}(P)\) holds at every \(v\in\mathcal F(P)\), then \(\operatorname{TCalm}_q(P)\) holds, so \(\Omega_P^{\to}(r)=O(r)\) and confidence-fiber excess is \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\). No endpoint-only condition is used.
statements.justification: This corollary preserves a classical sufficient route to root-\(n\) behavior.
statements.gap: Robinson1976 gives full-system stability, not a necessary projected criterion for the causal image.
statements.consumer: A full-fiber certificate is a simpler sufficient diagnostic for applied work.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{proj}}\), find necessary-and-sufficient intrinsic coderivative or projected-error-bound conditions for \(\operatorname{TCalm}_q(P)\) on the feasible observable-law model and compute the sharp semialgebraic H"older exponent of \(\Omega_P^{\to}(r)\) when calmness fails. Where a complete boundary representation is available, include cells on which \(\Delta_{\mathrm{WBC},C}(P)=0\). No necessity, noncalmness implication, singular example, generic regularity, or exponent formula is presupposed by discriminant vanishing.
statements.justification: The simple-root discriminant is only sufficient; the exact projected stability frontier and singular rates remain open.
statements.gap: Neither Robinson1976 nor the observable simple-root criterion characterizes projected calmness or the sharp H"older exponent on discriminant-zero cells.
statements.consumer: A solution would provide the quantitative geometry that the letter-tier existence result does not deliver.

sampling_model.design: Observational sampling from the fixed Wu--Bai--Cui SCM with districts \(\{\{A\},\{H,Y\},\{Z\},\{W\},\{M\}\}\).
sampling_model.overlap: The geometric theorem uses \(P(o)>0\); finite-sample honesty includes simplex faces.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The nuisance is the \(K\)-cell multinomial law; no bridge is estimated.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 3.1--3.3 identify the target through complete bridge equations.
The paper derives incomplete-proxy partial-identification bounds for causal effects.
Algorithm 2 constructs the program, Theorem 1 proves sharp equivalence, and Algorithm 3 gives anytime epsilon-sharp optimization.
Theorem 4.5 treats effective stratification of real algebraic maps, and Theorem 5.4 treats full semialgebraic sets.
The paper establishes finite semialgebraic partitions over which a semialgebraic mapping is locally trivial.
The abstract gives normalized Hausdorff and directed-Hausdorff limits and confidence collections for transformed Aumann expectations.
Theorem 3 gives root-n Hausdorff consistency of likelihood-ratio and Wald regions under Conditions R.
The page 633 abstract relates scalar Hellinger moduli to minimax risk and hardest two-point tests.
Section 3.2 and Theorem 3.1 with Corollary 3.1 use ordered scalar moduli for optimal confidence intervals over convex regression classes.
The paper develops uniform confidence regions for identified sets and their images.
The paper develops exact inference for scalar multinomial functionals.
The paper gives stability conditions for nonlinear inequality-system solution sets.

tldr: This angle closes as a coherent letter-tier synthesis for the corrected five-district Wu--Bai--Cui response program. Hardt1980 and the effective machinery of HelmerLeykinNanda2023, Theorem 4.5 and Theorem 5.4, imply together with quantifier elimination that a finite semialgebraic partition with compatible fiber-boundary descriptions exists; only conditional on a complete unrestricted square-free boundary representation and a nonzero leading-coefficient--discriminant test does the implicit-function argument yield projected Hausdorff calmness and root-\(n\) upper enlargement. No such WBC representation or exhaustion certificate is supplied here. Duarte sharpness, certified optimization, exact whole-set coverage, and the two-law Le Cam transfer remain supporting results.

project_justification.gap: Hardt local triviality and effective stratification guarantee finite geometric organization but do not provide the computed WBC eliminant, observable guards, discriminant evaluation, or projected Hausdorff bound required for a field-tier result.
project_justification.niche: Binary proxies are incomplete for a three-state witness, so a complete unrestricted boundary certificate would make local inferential regularity observable.
project_justification.fill: This letter-tier synthesis specializes the general semialgebraic existence results to the corrected WBC graph, states the quantitative implication conditionally, and records that the full-fiber certificate needed to instantiate it remains missing.

related_work: WuBaiCui2026 fixes the graph, target, bridge benchmark, and NLSY97 consumer. MiaoGengTchetgen2018 supplies the finite-rank interpretation, and GhassamiShpitserTchetgen2023 informs incomplete-proxy bounds. DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024 supplies Algorithm 2 for program construction, Theorem 1 for sharp equivalence, and Algorithm 3 for anytime optimization; the response-function correspondence here is only a graph-and-query specialization. HelmerLeykinNanda2023 already supplies effective stratification machinery: Theorem 4.5 treats real algebraic maps and Theorem 5.4 treats full semialgebraic sets. Hardt1980 supplies finite semialgebraic partitions with locally trivial fibers. Neither source supplies a computed WBC eliminant, complete observable guards, a discriminant evaluation, or a projected Hausdorff bound, and Hardt triviality alone is not quantitative Lipschitz control. BeresteanuMolinari2008, abstract, derives square-root-\(n\) Hausdorff and directed-Hausdorff limits and confidence collections in its SVRV/Aumann-expectation class. ChernozhukovKocatulumMenzel2015, pages 310, 328, and 340 and Theorem 3, derives weighted directed-Hausdorff and Wald regions and root-\(n\) Hausdorff consistency under its stated hypotheses. DonohoLiu1991, page 633 abstract, treats scalar Hellinger moduli and testing; ArmstrongKolesar2018, Section 3.2 and Theorem 3.1 with Corollary 3.1, treats ordered scalar moduli and optimal or minimax confidence intervals over convex regression classes. None computes the full-fiber WBC boundary artifact for this nonlinear, potentially disconnected causal image. SachsGabrielFay2024 and RomanoShaikh2010 inform confidence inversion; Robinson1976 supplies only a sufficient full-fiber stability route.
technical_internal_limitation: The v3 strengthening route required a nonconstant full-fiber eliminant factor, complete \(P\)-only sign guards, an exact nonzero discriminant evaluation, active response-code supports with masses, and a machine-checkable branch-exhaustion or Positivstellensatz artifact; the v4 core supplied none of them. The \(HY\) district has \(150{,}994{,}944\) deterministic response codes, so a selected response face or hand-written branch list cannot certify the unrestricted sharp set; generic CAD termination is not evidence that this computation was completed. No equality \(\Theta(P)=[\min\Theta(P),\max\Theta(P)]\) is asserted without connectedness. CAD certificates use real-algebraic witnesses with isolating intervals and sign certificates plus rational objective brackets, not unproved rational optimizer coordinates.
honest_scope: This v5 core is a coherent letter-tier synthesis and the terminal record of an unsuccessful full-fiber-artifact route; it does not reach field tier. The semialgebraic partition and compatible boundary-description claim is an existence and algorithmic corollary of quantifier elimination, Hardt local triviality, and effective stratification. The Hausdorff-Lipschitz conclusion is conditional on a complete unrestricted boundary representation and a nonzero leading-coefficient--discriminant test, neither of which is supplied. Discriminant vanishing implies no noncalmness, jump, singular rate, or H"older exponent. Coverage and the two-law transfer cover the feasible model, while full-fiber Robinson regularity remains only sufficient. No positive-cell singular example, regular uniform-law certificate, generic regularity claim, or rank-two contraction theorem is asserted.
seeds: next-angle target-specific bridge invariance below completeness

novelty_justification.prior_stratification: HelmerLeykinNanda2023 already supplies effective stratification machinery for real algebraic maps in Theorem 4.5 and full semialgebraic sets in Theorem 5.4; Hardt1980 already supplies finite semialgebraic partitions with locally trivial fibers.
novelty_justification.residual_contribution: The desired residual WBC contribution would be a computed unrestricted endpoint eliminant with complete observed-law guards, an exact nonzero discriminant evaluation, and branch exhaustion sufficient for the projected Hausdorff bound. This proposal does not deliver that result.
novelty_justification.closest_results: DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024 supplies the sharp response program; BeresteanuMolinari2008 and ChernozhukovKocatulumMenzel2015 are the closest set-inference results; DonohoLiu1991 and ArmstrongKolesar2018 are the closest modulus results.
novelty_justification.strict_gap: No cited source computes the unrestricted five-district WBC fiber boundary into an observable guarded polynomial criterion, and this closeout supplies no artifact that closes that gap.
novelty_justification.why_not_relabeling: The unconditional claim retained here is only the graph-specialized existence corollary. A field-tier advance would require full-fiber branch exhaustion and a quantitative Hausdorff argument, which remain missing.

message: Created and verified the non-identical v5 letter-tier closeout. It records the unsuccessful full-fiber-artifact route, preserves all SCM soundness repairs, corrects the Helmer–Leykin–Nanda and Hardt attributions, and includes the target-specific bridge-invariance handoff. Schema, proposal gate, symbol preflight, prose checks, and 70 targeted tests pass.
